APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 9, 2024

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Dr. Julia Ruedas, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Marisol Cortez, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Martin Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – absent
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Richard Rojo, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Councilmember Puente  6-0 (Councilmember Herrera absent)

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through 4.5.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:02 p.m. Councilmember Herrera joined the City Council in Closed Session. Mayor
  Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at approximately
  7:23 p.m.

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Existing Litigation – Pablo Ramos, et al. vs. City
  of El Monte, et al., LASC Case No. 22STCV19940.

  No final reportable action taken.

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) –
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  No final reportable action taken.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 9, 2024

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 – Conference with
  Legal Counsel – Discussion Regarding Annual City Manager Performance
  Evaluation Pursuant to Section 8 of Employment Contract.

  Title: City Manager

  No final reportable action taken.

  4.4  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiator.

  City Representative: City Attorney

  Unrepresented Employee: City Manager

  No final reportable action taken.

  4.5  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; and El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma Martinez, City Manager and Rigoberto
  Gutierrez, Human Resources/Risk Management Director.

  No final reportable action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 9, 2024

  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Update on Energy Efficiency Project Proposal.

  Mayor Ancona – Requested an update on this item. Advised that the project is
  ready for posting and ready to be brought to the City Council for consideration.
  Inquired when the item will be coming to the City Council for consideration as this
  was a directive given by the entire City Council.

  City Manager Martinez – Advised that she will bring back an update to the City
  Council. Will work with the Acting Public Works Director to understand the project
  deals. Will try to get it on in February.

  City Attorney Olivarez – Advised that the City Attorney’s Office will work with the
  City Manager to bring this to the City Council. Notice will need to be posted at least
  14 days prior to the Public Hearing.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Thanked the City Attorney’s Office for their
  support and guidance to bring this item to the City Council.

  Councilmember Herrera – Agreed that the City Manager be allowed to bring herself
  up to speed.

  18A.2 Discussion on Resident Utility Costs.

  Mayor Ancona – The City Council received an email from a resident regarding a
  utility bill. What Department can be a resource to the community to address these
  issues.

  City Manager Martinez – Requested that these issues be referred to her office in
  order to work with the appropriate Departments.

  Mayor Ancona – Asked that when these issues are referred to the City Manager
  that the City Manager provide a response to the City Council acknowledging
  receipt and also advise how the issues were resolved.

  Councilmember Cortez – Inquired if the City has a right to get involved in a private
  matter?

  City Manager Martinez – Advised that when it comes to private matters the City
  refers tenants to Legal Aid.

  18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Dr. Julia Ruedas

  18B.1 Update Regarding Empty Lots in District 3.

  Mayor Pro Tem Dr. Ruedas – Requested a report to the entire City Council in
  regards to all of the empty lots/vacant properties in the City broken down by
  District. Requested that the report include the status of each of the properties as
  far as contact with the owners.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – Requested that the list be provided to the entire
  City Council.

  10
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 9, 2024

  Councilmember Puente – Inquired what the proposed purpose or use of the data
  is.

  Mayor Ancona – Asked if the Ordinance was updated with regards to Empty Lots.
  Asked if there is language in the City’s code for properties that have been vacant
  for a long period of time to be able to impose fees.

  City Manager Martinez – There is an Ordinance and that is what staff is using to
  do the enforcement. There are two (2) nuisance properties that are being worked
  on by staff. There is no language currently in the City’s code to address this.

  Councilmember Cortez – Vacant lots are not attractive, due to covid a lot of
  landlords are struggling to attract new tenants.

  18B.2 Discussion Regarding a Health and Wellness Fair.

  Mayor Pro Tem Dr. Ruedas – Chronic illness continues to affect the community.
  Provided statistics on chronic illnesses that are affecting the community.
  Requested consensus to have a wellness fair. Would like one big event

  Mayor Ancona – Maybe if the City can do a health and wellness fair in collaboration
  with the school districts. Staff could partner with the school districts for such an
  event.

  Councilmember Herrera – Maybe the City can make sure that consistent
  programming throughout the season is in place that addresses various health
  issues within the community at Farmer’s Market.

  Councilmember Cortez – Recommended that it would be a great opportunity for
  staff to send out an invitation to all of the health care providers in the community
  to come to the Farmer’s Market.

  City Manage Martinez – DEMBA is excited to help with this. Advised that there is
  Earth Day coming up and that this fair could be incorporated then.

  Councilmember Martinez Muela – As part of the Resource Fair there is a Health
  and Wellness component during that particular event. There is lack of access that
  needs to be addressed. We may want to take on an overarching campaign
  #healthyelmonte to have consistent activity for our community. Happy to work with
  you on this. May want to add this as an agenda item at the Parks & Recreation Ad
  Hoc meeting coming up for further discussion.

  Councilmember Puente – Informed the City Council that one of the things that was
  just introduced in the State of California is that Medical is now available to all
  people regardless of immigration status. This is important piece of information to
  get out to the community.

  City Manager Martinez – Need clear guidance as to whether the Council would like
  a continuum or one big event.

18D.  Councilman Martin Herrera
